author: WP11
summary: Explains why DIRECT2D (native Direct2D over Direct3D 11) and GDI (Win32 presentation of a CPU raster) are different delivery stacks, how GDI composes the Software family's 2D code, and what their evidence and release gate prove. The alpha.1-era text is broadly right on architecture but stale on workflows (both native jobs are manual), on test counts and on comparison-scene advice. libcna.com had only renderer-table rows and one internals paragraph; a new deep dive now carries the device, format, blend, recovery, presentation and evidence depth.

sections.heading: DIRECT2D: a different Windows delivery stack
GDI: Win32 presentation over the software renderer
Why shared code does not make the identities equivalent
Choosing and testing the Windows 2D paths

concepts.text: DIRECT2D and GDI share the Windows gate and a 2D scope but not an architecture: DIRECT2D issues native Direct2D (ID2D1DeviceContext) commands on a private Direct3D 11 device, while GDI copies a CPU-rasterised frame produced by the SOFTWARE family's 2D code into a Win32 window.
DIRECT2D implements RenderTarget2D but not multiple render targets or occlusion queries, and its 3D refusal comes from the shared unsupported-3D route rather than a family-local throw.
GDI implements RenderTarget2D, refuses MRT and occlusion queries, and rejects every 3D resource and draw explicitly with System::NotSupportedException from its own methods.

concepts.section: DIRECT2D: a different Windows delivery stack
concepts.text: DIRECT2D is not a simplified mode of DIRECTX11: it calls the Direct2D API, compiles no HLSL and has no shader stage; sprites become Direct2D bitmaps, image brushes or effect graphs.

concepts.section: DIRECT2D: a different Windows delivery stack
concepts.text: Under Wine the Direct2D tests use the environment's own built-in d2d1, d3d11 and dxgi and bypass the DXVK gate with CNA_D3D11_SKIP_DXVK_GATE=1, because substituting DXVK would change the delivery stack under test.
concepts.note: The source said every registered path skips the DXVK gate; at 009d40f5 the Wine route sets the skip variable, the Proton route uses its own wrapper, and Wine additionally needs CNA_DIRECT2D_SKIP_RENDER_TARGET_DECORATION and CNA_DIRECT2D_SKIP_ADVANCED_BLEND.

concepts.section: DIRECT2D: a different Windows delivery stack
concepts.text: Sprite and shape work is expressed through native Direct2D resources; RenderTarget2D is supported only as a Color, depth-less, non-mipmapped, single-sampled bitmap, and only one target can be bound.
concepts.note: Extended with the TARGET format, depth, mip and MSAA refusals not mentioned in the source.

concepts.section: DIRECT2D: a different Windows delivery stack
concepts.text: Effect-aware 3D methods end in the family's explicit 3D refusal instead of drawing a sprite-coloured triangle after discarding a stock-effect packet; under WarnAndStub they log once and return no-op objects.
concepts.note: The WarnAndStub behaviour is a TARGET qualification the source omitted.

concepts.text: The native-Windows workflow d3d-windows-ci.yml runs the Direct2D label with the Direct3D 11 debug layer, repeats Direct2D_Lifetime on forced WARP and fails on any live object outside the debug-log whitelist; it runs only on manual dispatch.
concepts.note: The source implied an ordinary CI tier; the job is workflow_dispatch-only at 009d40f5.

concepts.text: The five Direct2D CTest gates are Direct2D_Smoke, Direct2D_2DParity, Direct2D_Lifetime, Direct2D_Soak and the device-free Direct2D_Unit GoogleTest filter.

Direct2D's release gate (validate_direct2d_plan.py --release-gate) stays blocked until a recorded native x64 Windows run and a physical non-96-DPI presentation capture exist; a workflow definition or a hosted hidden-window pass cannot satisfy it.

target.evidence: docs/direct2d-release-gate.md (CNA prose); docs/direct2d-native-evidence.md and docs/direct2d-physical-presentation-evidence.md absent at 009d40f5

concepts.text: A Direct2D failure report must say whether it ran on native Windows or on Wine/Proton built-ins and whether presentation, readback or only off-screen rendering was observed; a clean device construction proves neither pixel output nor the release gate.

concepts.section: GDI: Win32 presentation over the software renderer
concepts.text: GdiRenderer derives directly from IGraphicsRenderer and privately owns a GdiSoftware2DCore adapter; the build publishes a reviewed subset of Software translation units (CNA_GDI_SOFTWARE_SOURCES), no Software renderer pointer escapes, and a future Software 3D virtual cannot appear in GDI's vtable.

concepts.section: GDI: Win32 presentation over the software renderer
concepts.text: GDI's CPU path has a real standalone 8-bit stencil plane and an opt-in exact 4x CPU MSAA mode (four samples on a 2x2 grid, requested count 4 only) but no depth buffer; StencilBuffer, WireFrame, MSAA and AdditiveBlending answer true, DepthStencilBuffer false.

concepts.section: GDI: Win32 presentation over the software renderer
concepts.text: A GDI RenderTarget2D has colour, the stencil plane and an optional mip chain generated on unbind, deliberately no depth or MSAA attachment; one active target only, and SpriteBatch accepts only the fixed ColorMatrixEffect as a custom effect.

concepts.section: Why shared code does not make the identities equivalent
concepts.text: SOFTWARE runs windowless and returns pixels from its buffers while GDI must also create, update, invalidate and present a Win32 bitmap; a CPU raster test can miss stride, channel-order, invalidation or lifetime defects at the GDI boundary, and a present smoke cannot show stencil semantics.
tokens: stride, channel-order, invalidation or lifetime defect
concepts.note: The source spoke of depth or stencil semantics beneath the bitmap; GDI has no depth plane, so only stencil applies.

concepts.section: Why shared code does not make the identities equivalent
concepts.text: Every GDI renderer CTest is registered only inside if(NOT CMAKE_CROSSCOMPILING), so a Linux cross-build cannot run them; the native MSVC job gdi-windows-ci.yml (manual dispatch, hosted runner, hidden window) is the automated platform tier.
concepts.note: Nineteen GDI_* registrations at 009d40f5; the workflow is manual only and does not replace a visible DPI inspection.

concepts.section: Choosing and testing the Windows 2D paths
concepts.text: Choose DIRECT2D when native Direct2D resources and composition are the goal and GDI when a deterministic CPU image through the classic Win32 surface is valuable; neither is a route to programmable 3D.

target.evidence: cmake/RendererSelection.cmake (Windows gate); capability switches of both families

concepts.section: Choosing and testing the Windows 2D paths
concepts.text: A useful Windows 2D comparison scene includes alpha sprites, additive sprites where supported (GDI, not DIRECT2D), a clipped draw, a target round trip and a format-sensitive readback, plus stencil and MSAA probes for GDI, run both off-screen and through real presentation.
concepts.note: The source recommended additive sprites and depth probes for both; DIRECT2D refuses BlendState::Additive and GDI has no depth.

issues.text: DIRECT2D's constructor refuses any depth format other than DepthFormat::None, while GraphicsDeviceManager passes its PreferredDepthStencilFormat (default Depth24) unchanged; the family's example tests use the default manager.
DIRECT2D refuses BlendState::Additive and One/One with NotSupportedException and reports AdditiveBlending false.
Direct2D release gate blocked: no recorded native Windows run and no physical DPI capture exist; the native workflow is manual dispatch.
GDI CTests are never registered on cross-builds and gdi-windows-ci.yml is manual dispatch, so no automatic run exercises GDI.
